title: Nuevo Laredo Backs CBTIS Students With Cambridge English Path
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo signed on to a deal opening a path to Cambridge-backed English certification for students and teachers at CBTIS 137 and 234, with millions of pesos already invested in both campuses.
content:
Nuevo Laredo is backing students and teachers at CBTIS 137 and CBTIS 234 through a new collaboration agreement that opens a path to international English certification backed by the University of Cambridge, with Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal serving as honor witness at the signing, according to El Gráfico Tamaulipas.

The framework agreement was signed between the Legislative Liaison Office for Wellbeing and the Tamaulipas state office of DGETI, the federal agency for industrial and services technological education, and is meant to benefit students and teachers at both campuses directly, the newspaper reported.

Beyond the agreement itself, the city has already put more than 7 million pesos into CBTIS 137 for a perimeter wall and a roof structure, and more than 3 million pesos into CBTIS 234 for classroom expansion and electrical rehabilitation of the Center for Attention to Students with Disabilities (CAED), according to the report. An earlier wall at CBTIS 234 cost 1,374,808 pesos.

About 100 teachers at the two schools also benefit from the city’s Apoyo al Trabajo Docente program, which recognizes their work with an economic bonus, the newspaper reported.

The signing was led by Cruz Alberto Sainz Hernández, education liaison for the Legislative Liaison Office for Wellbeing; Olegario Muñiz Cura, DGETI commissioner in Tamaulipas; state Deputy Francisco Adrián Cruz Martínez; Faryde Yakabeth Ayech García, representing the University of Cambridge; and Mayor Canturosas Villarreal. CBTIS 137 director Paula Delhi Solis Quezada and CBTIS 234 director Antonio Guillén López also attended.

Sources: El Gráfico Tamaulipas, Nov. 19, 2026.
